title: Endpoint editor
summary: Add or change a serial port, TCP connection, folder or SFTP server.

sections.title: Kind and connection
paragraphs: The kind decides the settings and cannot be changed later; the id is fixed once saved. Serial: the port, baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits and flow control, as set on the instrument. TCP client: the host and port to connect to. TCP listener: the address to listen on and the port. Idle timeout drops a silent connection after that many seconds (0 is off); keepalive detects a vanished peer.

sections.title: Serial port
paragraphs: Choose a port the engine finds on its computer, or type any name, even one not plugged in. A port marked “used by” another endpoint cannot be opened by both. Refresh looks again.

sections.title: Who may connect
paragraphs: List the addresses or ranges allowed to connect to a listener. With none, a listener reachable from the network refuses to start unless Allow any peer to connect is ticked.

sections.title: Folders and SFTP servers
paragraphs: A folder is read when it is a channel's source and written when it is a destination; use two endpoints for separate in and out folders. Mode is watch for new files or poll on a schedule. File name pattern matches names only: * and ? are wildcards, such as *.csv. An SFTP server also needs a user name, a remote path, a poll interval and the host key fingerprint; a server showing a different key is refused.
An SFTP password or private key is never typed here: enter the name of a secret and set its value in Settings › Secrets.

sections.title: Test connection
paragraphs: Test connection tries the settings as typed, step by step with times. It only opens, connects or reads; a folder test also creates and deletes one empty hidden file. No data is sent and nothing is changed.

sections.title: Saving
paragraphs: Changing an endpoint restarts every channel that uses it. An endpoint that channels use cannot be deleted. To check and apply, see Saving and versions help.
